styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, tea houses and the old geisha streets.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Bamboo groves, riverside walks and hillside gardens.

stays.why: Best base for first-timers: bullet trains, buses and the subway all start here. Easy day trips to Nara and Osaka.
Central shopping and dining. Walk to Gion, Pontocho and Nishiki Market; good bus links.
Old wooden streets and lantern-lit lanes. Quiet at night, close to Kiyomizu-dera and Yasaka Shrine.
Bamboo grove and river views on your doorstep. Calm and green, but a train ride from the center.

food: Try Kyoto home cooking (obanzai) and yudofu, a simple hot-pot tofu dish served at temple restaurants.
Nishiki Market is a covered food street: graze on pickles, tamagoyaki and skewers. Many stalls close by late afternoon.
Kaiseki is the city's fine-dining tradition. Lunch sets cost far less than dinner; book ahead.
Matcha everything: tea, sweets and soft serve in Uji and around the temples.
Standing noodle bars and ramen shops near Kyoto Station are cheap and fast, often under ¥1000 a bowl.
more_time: Swap a temple morning for a day trip to Nara: about 45 minutes by train, with deer park and the Great Buddha.
Add Uji for green tea and the Byodo-in temple, roughly 30 minutes by train from Kyoto Station.
Fushimi Inari's full hill walk takes 2–3 hours. Go early morning to beat the crowds.

recommend.why: Three nights lets you see the eastern temples, Arashiyama and a day trip without rushing.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 8°C, lows around -1°C. Dress in layers; some sights are outdoor-only.
Still cold, highs near 9°C. Fewer crowds; plum blossoms start late in the month.
Mild and warming, highs near 14°C. Cherry blossom season nears; expect busy weekends.
Peak blossom month, highs near 19°C. Book hotels early; parks and temples are packed.
Green and pleasant, highs near 23°C. Good balance of weather and crowds.
Rainy season begins: about 15 rain days. Pack a compact umbrella and waterproof shoes.
Hot and humid, highs near 30°C with 18 rain days. Start sightseeing early; rest midday.
Hottest month, highs near 32°C and muggy nights. Carry water; use buses and taxis.
Still warm at 28°C with 15 rain days. Typhoon season: check forecasts before day trips.
Comfortable autumn, highs near 22°C. Leaves start turning late in the month.
Best month for foliage, highs near 16°C, only 7 rain days. Very busy at popular temples.
Cool and crisp, highs near 11°C. Quieter streets; pack a warm coat for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold, dry winters, a hot humid summer and a rainy spell in June–July. Spring and autumn are the best times to walk.

items.title: Best time: spring and autumn
items.text: April and November bring mild days around 16–22°C and the famous blossoms and leaves. Book early.

items.title: Hot, humid summer
items.text: July and August reach 30–32°C with many rain days. Sightsee at sunrise and rest in the afternoon.

items.title: Rainy season in June–July
items.text: Around 15–18 rain days. Showers are often short; a small umbrella is enough.

items.title: Cold, dry winter
items.text: January lows near -1°C. Days are clear and quiet; temples are far less crowded.

items.title: Autumn is the busiest
items.text: November has only about 7 rain days but huge crowds at maple spots. Go early morning.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, a light rain jacket, and layers for cool mornings. Add a warm coat for December–February.

transit.best: Buses and the two subway lines cover most sights; walk or cycle the temple districts.

modes.text: Two lines, Karasuma and Tozai, cover central Kyoto. Fares ¥220–330.
City buses reach most sights. Flat fare ¥230; a day pass costs ¥700 and pays off after three rides.
Metered taxis; GO and Uber apps operate. Handy for late nights and heavy rain.
Not recommended. Parking is scarce and expensive; public transport is easier.
Ideal for temples and backstreets. Bike rentals from ¥1000 a day.
